## feature

### v0.5.0 published carrying the snake_case rename

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The release workflow concluded success, the GitHub Release is Latest with both artifacts, the curated notes (led by the migration table) replaced the auto-generated body, and `sam-tagger --version` reported 0.5.0 before tagging.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Version bumped in the three files; commit `ec83436`; annotated tag `v0.5.0`; `main` + tag pushed (`2a1e95f..ec83436`).
2. Release note leads with the silent-failure warning and the verbatim BREAKING CHANGE migration table, per the standing recommendation.

#### before

The rename sat unreleased on `main` after `c968490`; version-pinned consumers still saw PascalCase values.

#### after

v0.5.0 is the Latest release; upgraders land on the migration table first.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

```text
   2a1e95f..ec83436  main -> main
 * [new tag]         v0.5.0 -> v0.5.0
workflow: conclusion=success  displayTitle="chore(release): bump version to 0.5.0"
assets: sam_tagger-0.5.0-py3-none-any.whl, sam_tagger-0.5.0.tar.gz
release list: v0.5.0  Latest  2026-10-21T02:30:18Z
sam-tagger --version → 0.5.0
```

:::

## caveat

### release-creation race between `gh` and the workflow

```
level: low
```

#### reason

The workflow's `contents: write` permission auto-created the release on tag push before my `gh release create` ran (`Release.tag_name already exists`); the fix was `gh release edit` with the curated notes.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. For future releases, expect the workflow to create the release object; edit rather than create, or delay creation until after the workflow finishes.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

```text
gh release create → "Release.tag_name already exists"
gh release view → body_len 86, assets already attached
gh release edit → curated notes in place
```

:::

None

## conclusion

### minor-with-breaking follows the repo's 0.x convention

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The precedent is in-repo: the TOML→CSV `refactor!` shipped as v0.2.0; this `refactor!` ships as v0.5.0.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. v0.4.0 → v0.5.0, one breaking change, no other deltas — the compare link in the notes states this.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- Release: https://github.com/jiangyun-fun/sam-tagger/releases/tag/v0.5.0
- Compare: https://github.com/jiangyun-fun/sam-tagger/compare/v0.4.0...v0.5.0

:::
